newsitem.title: USA: US Spot Prods - Prices ease with NYMEX, diffs hold.
newsitem.headline: US Spot Prods - Prices ease with NYMEX, diffs hold.

text.p: U.S. spot refined products prices eased slightly midday Tuesday with NYMEX futures on news Iraq expected to resume oil exports in the next week to 10 days, but cash differentials were little changed in spotty trade.
July NYMEX gasoline fell 0.19 cent, to 55.45 cents a gallon, while July heating oil dipped 0.12 cent to 51.80 cents at 1217 EST (1617 GMT).
Traders were awaiting release late afternoon of new weekly inventory data from the American Petroleum Institute.

Few gasoline deals were spotted, with "M2" conventional unleaded remaining offered at 3.0 cents below July futures and "A2" reformulated 87-octane languishing at 0.50 cent below the print, players said.

"With reformulated so low, why would you want to sell it unless you really have to. If you have it in tank, you might as well hold on to it," said one East Coast trader, who added that negative diffs on reformulated were rare in the summer driving season.
"Domestic guys (refineries) are pumping gasoline so strong," he added, that oversupply has been inevitable desite decent demand in recent weeks.

The market shrugged off an announcement earlier Tuesday by Sun Co that it would take down its 15,000 barrel per day reformer at its refinery in Marcus Hook, Pennsylvania, for a 20-day turnaround beginning July 18.
Prompt NYH heating oil, meanwhile, was offered at 0.30 cent below the screen, stable with Monday, while low sulfur diesel firmed a trace to a half cent over, traders said.
USG prompt front-19th-cycle "M1" gasoline was offered at 3.15 cents below the July screen, a tad weaker than Monday diffs, while prompt "A1" reformulated saw diffs hold at 1.25 cents under.
"The overall gasoline supply balance is heavy, so unless there are outages or a refiner needs something, differentials will probably be stable or head lower," one Gulf player said.
USG prompt back-18th heating oil, meanwhile, held steady at 2.25 cents under the screen, with low sulfur diesel also stable at 1.75 cents under, traders said.

Gasoline differentials were stable to weaker in a market where many players seem to have covered their positions for the month. Prompt conventional unleaded in Group Three was pegged 4.75/5.00 cents over July NYMEX, with any month barrels done at 4.50 cents and 4.25 cents, traders said.
Chicago unleaded came in slightly weaker at 0.75/1.00 cent over the print. Any months were talked 0.50/0.75 cents.
"It's pretty quiet," said a Group Three trader.
Meanwhile, low sulphur in Chicago was up a quarter cent to 1.25/1.50 cents over NYMEX heating oil amid the start of agricultural demand in Illinois and Indiana.
